entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Najm al-Dīn Umāra al-Ḥakamī al-Yamanī was a Sunni historian, jurist and poet of Yemen of great repute who was closely associated with the late Fatimid Caliphate of Egypt. He was executed by order of Saladin at Cairo on April 6, 1174 for his part in a conspiracy to restore Fatimid rule. His Tarikh al-Yaman is the earliest, and in respects the most important, history of Yemen from the Islamic era. Umara ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Yamani was a journalists & chroniclers from Q20404530 (1121, Q20404530–1174-04-13). historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent historian and jurist of the late Fatimid Caliphate, Umara ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Yamani's Tarikh al-Yaman is a crucial primary source for understanding Yemen's history during the Islamic era. Its significance extends beyond Yemen, as it provides valuable insights into the politics and culture of the region.
